slides.texte_overlay:
5 strange hobbies to make you
disguistingly intelligent

reading old letters

read published letters from famous people in history. private letters show how great minds actually thought, doubted and changed their opinions over time.

identifying clouds

learn the names of ten cloud types and spot them on your walks. it trains your eye for patterns and turns every look at the sky into a small science lesson.

translating songs

translate the lyrics of a song in a language you don't speak. you learn words, grammar and culture at once, and you'll never hear that song the same way again.

a lesson a day

spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in a subject you've never touched: astronomy, philosophy, architecture. strange subjects stretch your brain in new directions.
slides.texte_sophia:
a lesson a day

i used to only learn about my own field. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: astronomy, philosophy, architecture. strange subjects stretch the brain.

slides.texte_overlay:
building puzzles in your head

before sleep, mentally walk through your home and place every object. it sounds odd, but it's one of the oldest memory exercises and it works surprisingly well.
